extracted.intended_audience: school and college administrators, Title IX Coordinators, investigators/decision-makers, and legal counsel responsible for implementing Title IX grievance procedures
extracted.subtask_short: Title IX grievance & supportive measures rules
extracted.subtask_description: Interpretation and implementation rules for supportive measures, emergency removal, grievance procedures, and terminology under the Department of Education's Title IX final regulations. Focused on what recipients (elementary/secondary and postsecondary) must and may do when responding to allegations of sexual harassment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on imposing non-supportive disciplinary actions without §106.45 process
rubrics_metrics.description: A recipient must refrain from imposing disciplinary sanctions or other actions that are not supportive measures, against a respondent, without following the §106.45 grievance process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If an action is disciplinary (as described/listed in the recipient's grievance process), it may not be taken as a supportive measure prior to following §106.45. The grievance process provides due process protections and must be followed before imposing disciplinary sanctions or non-supportive actions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grievance process must describe range of possible disciplinary sanctions and supportive measures
rubrics_metrics.description: The recipient's grievance process must describe the range, or list, the disciplinary sanctions that a recipient might impose following a determination of responsibility, and describe the range of supportive measures available to complainants and respondents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The listed disciplinary sanctions constitute actions the recipient considers 'disciplinary' and therefore not supportive measures. Whether an action may be taken as a supportive measure depends on whether it is disciplinary/punitive or unreasonably burdens the respondent if not listed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Listed disciplinary actions cannot be used as supportive measures before process
rubrics_metrics.description: If a recipient has listed ineligibility to play on a sports team or hold student government as a possible disciplinary sanction, the recipient may not take that action against a respondent without first following §106.45.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conversely, if the recipient's grievance process does not describe an action as a possible disciplinary sanction, whether it may be taken as a supportive measure is determined by whether it is non-disciplinary/non-punitive and does not unreasonably burden the respondent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Certain actions are inherently disciplinary and cannot be supportive measures
rubrics_metrics.description: Certain actions, such as suspension or expulsion from enrollment, or termination from employment, are inherently disciplinary, punitive, and/or unreasonably burdensome and so will not constitute a 'supportive measure' whether or not listed in the grievance process pursuant to §106.45(b)(1)(vi).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipients should treat such inherently disciplinary actions as requiring the formal grievance process before imposition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Emergency removal authority (§106.44(c)/(d)) with immediate notice and challenge
rubrics_metrics.description: The Department reiterates that a recipient may remove a respondent from all or part of a recipient's education program or activity in an emergency situation pursuant to §106.44(c) (with or without a grievance process pending) and may place a non-student employee respondent on administrative leave during a grievance process, pursuant to §106.44(d).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A recipient must provide the respondent with notice and an opportunity to challenge the emergency removal decision immediately following the removal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Obligation to conclude grievance within a reasonably prompt time frame
rubrics_metrics.description: A recipient is obligated to conclude a grievance process within a reasonably prompt time frame, thus limiting the duration of time for which supportive measures serve to maintain a status quo while a grievance is pending.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prompt resolution limits prolonged interim measures and balances equal educational access of both parties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Elementary/secondary quick interventions may be non-punitive supportive measures
rubrics_metrics.description: In elementary and secondary school contexts, many common actions (educational conversations, sending students to principal's office, changing seating/class assignments) are not inherently punitive or disciplinary and therefore do not violate the §106.30 definition of supportive measures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such actions are permitted to maintain order, protect safety, and counsel students. By contrast, expulsions and suspensions are disciplinary and require the §106.45 grievance process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Final regulations apply only to conduct that meets §106.30 sexual harassment definition
rubrics_metrics.description: These final regulations apply to conduct that constitutes sexual harassment as defined in §106.30, and not to every instance of student misbehavior.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipients should not conflate ordinary misbehavior with conduct governed by Title IX sexual harassment provisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: No requirement to lift supportive measures after a finding of non-responsibility
rubrics_metrics.description: These final regulations do not expressly require a recipient to continue providing supportive measures upon a finding of non-responsibility, and the Department declines to require recipients to lift, remove, or cease supportive measures upon a finding of non-responsibility; recipients retain discretion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A determination of non-responsibility may reflect insufficient evidence, not falsity of allegations. Recipients may continue or alter supportive measures for complainants or respondents; supportive measures by definition do not punish or unreasonably burden the other party.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recipients may design their own process for requesting/granting supportive measures (with essential Title IX Coordinator duties)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Department declines to require a specific process for requesting/granting supportive measures so recipients have flexibility to develop processes consistent with their administrative structure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Despite recipient flexibility, §106.44(a) requires the Title IX Coordinator to promptly contact complainant to discuss availability of supportive measures, consider complainant's wishes, inform about availability with or without a formal complaint, and explain how to file a formal complaint.

rubrics_metrics.name: Title IX Coordinator must coordinate effective implementation of supportive measures
rubrics_metrics.description: The final regulations prescribe that a recipient's Title IX Coordinator must remain responsible for coordinating the effective implementation of supportive measures, so the burden of arranging and enforcing supportive measures remains on the recipient, not on any party.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipients may designate more than one employee as Title IX Coordinator if needed. Title IX Coordinators often rely on other offices to provide measures but must serve as point of contact and ensure implementation so the student is not burdened with navigating internal processes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mutual no-contact orders are an illustrative supportive measure (one-way not categorically prohibited)
rubrics_metrics.description: The inclusion of 'mutual restrictions on contact between the parties' in §106.30 is illustrative, not exhaustive. The inclusion does not mean one-way no-contact orders are never appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A fact-specific inquiry is required to determine whether a one-way no-contact order meets the §106.30 supportive measures definition. One-way orders could be appropriate (e.g., to enforce a court restraining order) provided they do not unreasonably burden the other party.

rubrics_metrics.name: No-contact order scope requires fact-specific, burden-sensitive analysis
rubrics_metrics.description: Further restrictions, such as avoiding physical proximity between the parties, will require a fact-specific analysis to determine the scope of a no-contact order that deters sexual harassment without unreasonably burdening the other party.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: where both parties are athletes, consider limiting scope to deter harassment while not forcing either party to forgo educational activities. Options include mutual communication bans, alternate housing (without cost to complainant), or other tailored measures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mutual restrictions on contact do not automatically constitute unlawful retaliation
rubrics_metrics.description: The Department does not believe that 'mutual restrictions on contact between the parties' could constitute unlawful retaliation by restricting the complainant's participation as well as the respondent's.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Supportive measures must be non-disciplinary and non-punitive; actions taken under guise of supportive measures that penalize the complainant to discourage exercising Title IX rights would constitute unlawful retaliation under §106.71.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supportive measures list is illustrative and not exhaustive; can include restorative measures
rubrics_metrics.description: The Department encourages recipients to broadly consider measures to ensure equal access, including measures designed to retrospectively 'restore' (e.g., retake class/exam, transcript addendum) or prospectively 'preserve' equal educational access. The §106.30 illustrative list includes course-related adjustments that could encompass such measures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipients are not precluded from providing supportive measures not listed; consider both prospective and remedial actions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supportive measures must be non-disciplinary, non-punitive, and not unreasonably burden others
rubrics_metrics.description: The second sentence of §106.30 clarifies that supportive measures must be designed to restore or preserve equal access and must not unreasonably burden the other party, which may include measures also designed to protect safety or the recipient's educational environment, or deter sexual harassment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If an action punishes or unreasonably burdens the complainant, it is not a supportive measure and may be retaliation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Terminology usage: prefer neutral procedural terms (complainant/respondent, decision-maker)
rubrics_metrics.description: The final regulations use neutral terms 'complainant' and 'respondent,' 'decision-maker' and 'determination regarding responsibility' to describe the grievance process rather than criminal/civil courtroom terms, to reflect administrative rather than criminal proceedings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department intentionally avoids terms like 'plaintiff/defendant' and generally does not use 'survivor'/'victim' in regulatory text to remain objective and impartial; remedies are mandated when a reliable determination shows a complainant was victimized.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of 'equal' versus 'equitable' is deliberate and context-dependent
rubrics_metrics.description: Where parties are given 'equal' opportunity both must be treated the same; where parties must be treated 'equitably' the regulations explain what equitable means for a complainant and respondent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Equal treatment does not require identical accommodations (e.g., translators only for parties who need them). The regulations use both terms thoughtfully.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of 'education program or activity' includes locations/events under recipient's substantial control and recognized student org buildings
rubrics_metrics.description: §106.44(a) specifies that for purposes of §§106.30, 106.44, and 106.45, an education program or activity includes locations, events, or circumstances over which the recipient exercised substantial control over both the respondent and the context in which the harassment occurs, and includes any building owned or controlled by a student organization officially recognized by a postsecondary institution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This definition aligns with Davis and clarifies when sporting activities, afterschool programs, or field trips are within a recipient's program or activity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of 'student' and applicability to applicants
rubrics_metrics.description: The existing definition (34 CFR 106.2(r)) defines 'student' as 'a person who has gained admission.' 'Admission' includes selection for any enrollment or membership; an admitted applicant is considered attempting to participate in the program.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The term 'person' or 'individual' is used elsewhere to ensure Title IX protections apply broadly; 'students' used where specific student-focused actions are required (e.g., notice of Title IX Coordinator).

rubrics_metrics.name: Impartiality requirement for Title IX personnel
rubrics_metrics.description: The final regulations require impartiality on the part of Title IX personnel (Title IX Coordinators, investigators, decision-makers, and persons who facilitate informal resolutions) to reinforce the truth-seeking purpose of a grievance process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treating parties with dignity, respect, and sensitivity without bias, prejudice, or stereotypes fosters impartiality. The Department acknowledges trauma-informed practices as a best practice but maintains impartiality as a required principle in Title IX processes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grievance process must provide robust due process protections
rubrics_metrics.description: The grievance process in §106.45 provides robust due process protections for both parties, and before imposition of any disciplinary sanctions or other actions that are not supportive measures as defined in §106.30 against a respondent, a recipient must follow a grievance process that complies with §106.45.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The grievance process is rooted in due process principles to create fair, reliable outcomes and is administrative in nature to effectuate Title IX purposes.
